_comment: Scenario-staged rout-then-ANNIHILATION demo: a lone low-morale (1) player infantry block of 12 is charged head-on by two 12-horse cavalry troops and BREAKS -- it enters routing (drawn faded) and flees. The squadrons are shallow and spawn close so their facing-front is in spatha reach at regiment contact. Routing units are still valid combat targets, and the cavalry (8.5 m/s sprint) are faster than the fleeing infantry (4.0 m/s sprint, 1.3 x that in flight), so pursuit is relentless: each routed man runs on his own from the riders he sees toward his own back edge (SoldierFlightStep), the runners scatter, and each rider rides at the runner nearest him and cuts him down on the move (SoldierPursuitStep; at Cannae the Numidian horse pursued the fleeing Roman cavalry and cut most of them down, Polybius 3.116). The casualties keep its morale from recovering, so it never rallies and is ANNIHILATED (soldiers reach zero) rather than escaping or rallying. The scene runs on a custom tall map (field 1600x2400, flat) with every actor staged in the deep south, so the flight has room; a second, safe player unit (140 Spearmen) stays in the fight so the battle doesn't declare defeat the instant the infantry routs. Measured with dense 2-tick FULL dumps on seeds 0 to 4, 2026-11-20 on #1949's branch: it routs at tick 60 and is still routing at tick 250 (pinned) with 4 to 8 of its 12 men left; the lead squadron (uid 3) is after it (target_enemy_uid 0) inside ticks 200 to 300 on every seed (pinned); and the last runner falls at tick 396 on the clip's own seed (seed 0), 582 on seed 1, 606 on seed 2 and 422 on seed 3. On seed 4 the riders ride the runners down only while their attack order on the company stands (SoldierTakeUp); the AI's order on it lapses for squadron uid 2 from tick 426 and uid 3 turns on the spearmen at tick 722, and the last runner outruns the pursuit and leaves the field north after tick 1200, so the absent window runs to tick 1300. On main c36560fa it was caught at tick 420, fought on the move to tick 542 and cut down between ticks 648 and 650. The pins were: ROUTING at tick 540, uid 3 targeting it and engaged in melee inside ticks 480 to 600, and gone inside ticks 610 to 700. The bottom-up flight and the riders' own pursuit (#1949) run it down earlier on four seeds and about as late on one, so the windows move to cover every seed, and the engaged pin is retired: riders who cut runners down on the move are not a block engaged in melee. Camera frames the clash and then pans with the chase (website/tools/demo-catalog.sh records 360 frames at 30 fps, to tick 720, which shows the kill on every seed). No player input needed. (A unit that truly breaks free instead recovers cleanly -- see test/unit/test_morale_recovery_demo_scenario.gd for that case in isolation.)

follow_error.reason: This is a regression from the riders' own pursuit (#1949), measured 2026-11-20 on dense 2-tick FULL dumps against 30: uid 2 reads 41.27, 29.06, 6.92, 34.65 and 224.71 on seeds 0 to 4 and uid 3 reads 29.87, 29.45, 5.90, 33.01 and 5.90, failing on seed 0 and 4 (uid 2) and seed 3 (uid 3); main 6d65b227 reads 17.57 (uid 2) and 31.75 (uid 3) on every seed. A squadron whose chase ends re-forms where its riders stand, on a grid laid at their centroid, and marches on while they walk to their places: uid 3 on seed 3 reads 29.3 to 32.4 from tick 674 to 722 as it marches on the spearmen, and uid 2 on seed 0 reads 40.1 to 41.0 at ticks 1166 to 1176 as it marches off the spearmen with 8 men left. A unit that falls in on its own men rather than on a laid grid is #1954. Seed 4's 224.71 is the moving wheel described under overlap, item 28 of #1950.

overlap.reason: This is a regression from the riders' own pursuit (#1949), measured 2026-11-20 on dense 2-tick FULL dumps: the second squadron (uid 2) reads 6.53, 6.77, 4.72, 8.93 and 0.53 on seeds 0 to 4 against 5, failing on seeds 2 and 4; main 6d65b227 reads 20.69 on every seed. On seed 2 two riders forming up where they stood when the chase ended (tick 194) come within 4.72 wu at tick 196: a rider who gives way to a crossing rider before contact is #1956. On seed 4 the chase ends at tick 434 when the AI's attack order lapses, the squadron re-forms where its riders stand and its next move order starts a moving wheel, which carries every rider rigidly about the hinge, men 300 wu off their places included, and two are carried within 0.53 wu: a wheel by men about a pivot man, not a grid swung about a hinge, is item 28 of #1950 (R0, R3).
